svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "Aerobic respiration: four stages, from glucose to ATP."], [1, "Glycolysis in the cytoplasm: glucose is split into two pyruvate; net 2 ATP."], [5, "Link reaction in the matrix: pyruvate \u2192 acetyl CoA, releasing CO\u2082."], [8, "Krebs cycle: carbon atoms leave as CO\u2082; reduced NAD and FAD carry hydrogen."], [12.5, "Oxidative phosphorylation: electrons pass along the chain; H\u207a flow through ATP synthase."], [16.5, "Oxygen accepts electrons and H\u207a to form water. Total about 30\u201332 ATP."]]
svg.title: Aerobic respiration
svg.desc: The stages of aerobic respiration: glycolysis in the cytoplasm, the link reaction and Krebs cycle in the mitochondrial matrix, and oxidative phosphorylation on the inner membrane, with carbon, ATP, NADH, CO2 and water.
svg.text: Per molecule of glucose. Black dots: carbon atoms.

g.data-info: Glucose (6C) is phosphorylated using 2 ATP, then split and oxidised to 2 pyruvate (3C). Net gain: 2 ATP and 2 reduced NAD per glucose. No oxygen needed.
Each pyruvate loses CO₂ (decarboxylation) and hydrogen (dehydrogenation), forming acetyl coenzyme A (2C) and reduced NAD.
Acetyl (2C) joins oxaloacetate (4C) to form citrate (6C). Each turn releases 2 CO₂ and makes 3 NADH, 1 FADH₂ and 1 ATP; two turns per glucose.

g.text: per glucose (2 turns): 4 CO₂, 6 NADH, 2 FADH₂, 2 ATP

g.data-info: Reduced NAD and FAD give electrons to the electron transport chain; the energy pumps H⁺ into the intermembrane space; H⁺ flow back through ATP synthase makes most of the ATP (chemiosmosis). Oxygen is the final electron acceptor, forming water.
About 30–32 ATP per glucose in aerobic respiration, compared with 2 in anaerobic respiration.
